name: Egyptian Mesaka’a With Eggplant and Tomato Sauce

ingredients.name: neutral oil, such as canola, for frying, divided
green bell peppers, stemmed, seeded, and coarsely chopped
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

instructions.primary_message: For the Vegetables: In a large skillet, heat 1/4 cup oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Meanwhile, place flour in a shallow bowl.

Working in batches, lightly dredge eggplant slices in flour, shaking off excess. Add dredged eggplant to the hot oil and fry until deeply golden brown on both sides, 1 to 2 minutes per side. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and sprinkle with 1/4 teaspoon salt. Repeat with remaining oil, eggplant, and salt, heating each addition of oil until shimmering before adding the next batch; set aside.
Add bell peppers and chiles (if using), to the remaining hot oil and cook until slightly softened but still bright green, about 1 minute. Transfer to paper towel-lined plate; set aside.

For the Garlicky Tomato Sauce: In a medium saucepan, heat oil over medium heat until shimmering. Add garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add vinegar and cook until slightly reduced, about 30 seconds.

Stir in passata or tomato purée, tomato paste, and 1/4 cup water, salt, cumin, Vegeta (if using), sugar (if using), and black pepper. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until flavors meld and sauce has slightly thickened, about 20 minutes.

To Assemble Mesaka’a: While sauce is cooking, adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Once sauce is off the heat, add eggplant, bell peppers, and chiles to tomato sauce and gently toss until lightly coated.
Transfer eggplant mixture to a 9 x 33-cm baking dish and bake until the sauce is bubbling and the vegetables are heated through, 20 to 25 minutes.
Let cool for 10 minutes. Serve hot, warm, or at room temperature with pita bread, if desired.

schema_metadata.keywords: Egyptian mesaka'a, mesaka'a, moussaka, Egyptian moussaka, eggplant recipe, fried eggplant, tomato sauce, Middle Eastern eggplant recipe, garlic tomato sauce, pita bread

description: Egyptian mesaka’a combines tender fried eggplant and peppers with a garlicky, tangy tomato sauce; it can be served hot, warm, or cold.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1 to 2 small chile peppers such as serrano or jalapeño, stemmed (optional); 1 teaspoon Vegeta seasoning (optional; see notes); 1/2 teaspoon sugar (optional); Warm pita bread for serving, optional

Optional substitutions: passata purée → tomato purée

Notes: Vegeta is an all-purpose seasoning created in Croatia and commonly used throughout the Balkans and parts of Central and Eastern Europe. Made with salt, dehydrated vegetables, spices, and MSG, it adds savory, vegetal depth to the tomato sauce. It is optional and can be omitted. It can be found in Eastern European grocery stores, some mainstream grocery stores, and online.

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days. To reheat, cover and warm in a 175°C (350°F) oven until heated through, about 15 to 20 minutes. Individual portions can be reheated in the microwave in 30-second intervals until hot.
author: Nermine Mansour
